article.title: Moving from Linux app cleanup to Mac storage review
article.intent: Help a CleanMyLinux user moving to a Mac separate package/app removal, app reset, rebuildable cache and original project data before choosing a workflow.
outline: Start with the target OS, not a list of interchangeable cleaners
Separate uninstalling an app from resetting its local state
Review project data and cache rebuild costs on the Mac
Inspect a Mac inventory before authorizing changes
Choose Linux package management or Mac investigation according to the machine
article.openingBoundary: CleanMyLinux is for Linux. Breathing Room, which we build, is a Mac preview, not a port of its uninstaller/updater.
article.interactionHandoff: A non-destructive decision checklist: target OS → package/app removal vs storage investigation → original vs rebuildable data → review permission and rebuild cost. No deletion buttons or invented savings.
visualOrder: Official CleanMyLinux Applications start screen immediately after lead
Current-source Breathing Room Space example-data view beside inventory discussion
notAllowed: Claiming Breathing Room replaces APT/DNF/Flatpak/Snap updating

comparison.title: CleanMyLinux vs Breathing Room: Linux and Mac roles
comparison.intent: Short OS-first decision, not a universal winner table.
comparison.linkPolicy: Verify counterpart/tool routes at drafting; no invented specific tool route.
comparison.conclusion: Stay with a Linux-native package workflow on Linux. On a Mac, evaluate a Mac storage/process workflow separately, including preview and hosted-service caveats.

cleanmylinux: Documented Linux package/app management across native formats, Flatpak and Snap; useful when that is the actual job.
MIT source and public beta download metadata can be inspected without an account.
Not a native Mac choice; unresolved distro minimums, beta naming and source/release feature boundaries must remain visible.
breathingRoom: Documented Mac storage exploration and grouped process/activity investigation; a different job from Linux package updating.
Free local core with optional paid hosted AI Care; neither all-local AI nor unlimited AI.
Non-notarized preview, Python prerequisite, untested physical Intel execution and incomplete clean-machine/binary parity evidence limit recommendations.
